environment_events: The old Delphi session displayed error 1400 and was restarted before the final GUI builds.
The first x64 packaging attempt ran out of space on C:. The packager removed its own incomplete staging tree; the successful retry used G: for staging.
Bulk and single-file cleanup of old C: audit deployments was rejected by the tool policy. Those old deployments were not removed through another mechanism.

A new-deployment cleanup guard initially encountered the library-created _myhomelib cache and stopped without deleting it. The cleanup now skips non-test names and removes only newly created, validated synthetic deployment roots after success.

The successful Win32 upgrade test ran on D:. Subsequent integration deployments used a fresh C: test root and were cleaned after success. The initial D: deployment was also removed after verifying its owned marker, archive hash and installed journal.

The first legacy installer-suite attempt used a tester compiled with the old application release constant; its feed-history assertion correctly detected the mismatch. The tester was rebuilt in Delphi for each architecture and the suite rerun without changing an assertion.
limitations: Both architectures were executed on this Windows x64 machine; no separate physical Windows x86 installation was tested.
Final-version reruns cover five affected native modes per architecture, not a second execution of the entire 54-mode audit after changing only the version.

Installer tests use synthetic personal data. Raw logs, fixture manifests and final release archives remain as local evidence. Disposable fixture copies and new integration roots were removed after success; paths and hashes are recorded.
